high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless Yoruba àdìrẹ ẹlẹ́kọ textile illustration: two women and one dye vat are built from flat indigo resist shapes as a prepared wrapper enters the bath, dye reaching only exposed regions; frontal geometry, deep indigo and cream, no gradients, realistic depth, writing, diagrams or arrows.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A continuous deep-indigo rectangular field is divided by cream resist borders into one large central working scene and narrow surrounding bands of abstract grids, interlaces, dots, and concentric rings. Every region remains flat and frontal, without horizon, sky, architectural room, window, realistic ground plane, perspective recession, inscription, letter, numeral, map, flag, crown, interface, caption, arrow, diagram, ranking device, throne, or modern machine.

elements.desc: Wide circular indigo vat occupying the lower center as a flattened dark-blue oval enclosed by one thick cream resist rim and two short rust supports. A single prepared wrapper descends through its opening; the vessel has no lid, gauge, label, emblem, control lever, separate compartment, decorative face, symbolic gate, realistic reflection, or modeled volume.

Adult Yoruba indigo dyer standing beside the vat, dark-brown skin, black hair wrapped in a plain indigo headcloth, cream blouse, rust wrapper, and bare forearms. With a focused neutral expression, she lowers the prepared cloth using both hands, acting only on this single wrapper and carrying no key, badge, staff, judging tool, or authority symbol.

Adult Yoruba resist artist standing across the vat, dark-brown skin, braided black hair gathered low, deep-blue blouse, cream-and-rust wrapper, and simple sandals. She holds an empty shallow cassava-paste bowl and a clean palm-rib applicator after completing the resist, watching the immersion without touching the dye or commanding the dyer.

Single two-panel cotton wrapper passing continuously from the dyer’s hands into the vat and rising across a simple cream support behind it. Dried pale cassava resist covers precise rectangular bands, interlaces, dots, and concentric rings; exposed regions are saturated indigo while every protected region remains cream, with no letters, numerals, portraits, crowns, logos, or explanatory symbols.
